papers.catalogue_title: The Validation Bottleneck: Alpha Discovery When Hypotheses Are Free
papers.title: The Validation Bottleneck: Alpha Discovery When Hypotheses Are Free
papers.label: Markets and quantitative finance
papers.abstract_html: Large language models have made investment hypotheses effectively free, moving the binding constraint on alpha discovery from generation to validation. Restricting a model’s data feed does not restrict its knowledge: it has read the anomaly literature, so its training cutoff is the only valid out-of-sample boundary. Put the two facts together and the strategies tested multiply without limit while the evidence that can judge them accrues at one year per year. Three consequences follow. The smallest alpha an allocator can certify rises with the logarithm of the number of strategies the industry tests, because the luckiest fluke among them looks better the more are tried. Alpha that decays faster than the evidence accrues cannot be certified within its own lifetime. And firms drawing hypotheses from the same model correlate their discoveries, on that model’s most celebrated ideas, before either holds a position. Two pre-registered experiments then measure the contamination and the bind. Told to propose predictors not yet in the literature as of a past date, five models across three lineages return that literature anyway: 26–55% of their “novel” proposals match predictors already in the library. Convergent rediscovery could explain that; it cannot explain the sign. The predictors they propose most often are those that performed worse afterward (combined z = −3.88). They reproduce fame, not future returns. Evaluated strictly after verified cutoffs, none of the roughly 900 evaluable strategies clears false-discovery control, and no model’s best pick beats the best of an equal number of random draws from the same restricted language; two of the three do worse. The models’ own stated predictions about their mechanisms held 39% of the time, against 70% for mechanisms already documented as true put through the same tests—and 46% against 86% on the one window long enough to test structure. By the second consequence, no window available today could certify a true strategy either: the nulls measure the window’s width, not the models’ quality. Hypotheses are free, and worth what they cost until validated.

papers.title: The AI-Native Asset Manager: Institutional Cognition as Competitive Advantage
papers.label: Markets and quantitative finance
papers.abstract_html: The asset management industry faces a structural inversion. As information becomes abundant, analysis cheap, and first-pass portfolio construction partially commoditized, the scarce resource shifts from intelligence to institutional epistemology-the architecture by which a firm generates, challenges, sizes, and learns from investment beliefs. This paper argues that the next generation of dominant asset managers will not be firms with better models in the narrow sense, but firms that have built a superior epistemic operating system: a machine-augmented cognitive architecture organized around the lifecycle of belief under uncertainty. We introduce a three-engine frameworknarrative intelligence for beta, statistical intelligence for cross-sectional alpha, and causal issuer intelligence for idiosyncratic opportunities-and show how AI enables their coordination into a single adaptive capital-allocation organism. We provide a concrete organizational blueprint, define new institutional performance metrics, and identify the governance constraints required to prevent epistemic pathologies in AI-augmented firms.

papers.abstract_html:
Hierarchical Risk Parity [López de Prado, 2016] and the Schur-complement generalisation of [Cotton, 2024] are among the most widely adopted regularised portfolio construction methods, yet both are signal-blind: they solve only the minimum-variance problem and cannot accommodate an arbitrary expected-return forecast. This paper introduces three methods that incorporate alpha signals into hierarchical and regularised portfolio construction.

HRP-μ\mu is a hierarchical allocator that accepts an arbitrary signal μ\mu and nests standard HRP when γ=0\gamma = 0 and μ=𝟏\mu=\mathbf{1}. It preserves the tree-based structure of HRP while extending it beyond the minimum-variance setting. HRP-Σμ\Sigma\mu strengthens this construction by replacing inverse-variance representatives with recursive local mean–variance optima, thereby using richer within-cluster covariance information at the same O(N2)O(N^2) asymptotic cost.

CRISP (Correlation-Regularised Iterative Shrinkage Portfolios) is an iterative solver for Pγw=μP_\gamma w = \mu with Pγ=(1−γ)diag⁡(Σ)+γΣP_\gamma = (1-\gamma)\operatorname{diag}(\Sigma) + \gamma \Sigma, so that γ\gamma interpolates between a diagonal portfolio rule and full Markowitz. At convergence, CRISP is Markowitz applied to a variance-preserving shrunk covariance—diagonal variances unchanged, off-diagonal correlations shrunk—with γ\gamma tuned for out-of-sample Sharpe rather than covariance-estimation loss.

In Monte Carlo experiments across multiple covariance regimes and estimation ratios, HRP-μ\mu and HRP-Σμ\Sigma\mu both outperform plain HRP—not only on general expected-return forecasts, where HRP is signal-blind, but also on the minimum-variance problem μ=𝟏\mu = \mathbf{1} that is HRP’s home territory—with HRP-Σμ\Sigma\mu consistently improving on HRP-μ\mu. CRISP at intermediate γ\gamma is the dominant method in both regimes, outperforming HRP, Cotton, Ledoit–Wolf shrinkage, direct Markowitz, and the signal-aware hierarchical methods at every sample size tested.

Keywords: portfolio optimization, hierarchical risk parity, Schur complement, signal-dependent allocation, covariance shrinkage, out-of-sample evaluation

papers.abstract_html: For every torus knot, the rank of the differential of the Daemi–Scaduto S-complex of singular instanton homology is determined by the signature and the Alexander polynomial; this follows from theorems of Li–Ye and Daemi–Scaduto. For the torus knots T(3,n)T(3,n) the differential has rank zero or one according to nn modulo 66, and its rank equals Daemi and Scaduto’s Frøyshov-type invariant; they proved this in two of the four residue classes and for n=4,5n=4,5, and Hedden, Herald and Kirk computed it for n≤38n\le38. Following Lewallen, Klassen and Hedden–Herald–Kirk, we describe the generators of the instanton complexes and their ℤ/4\mathbb{Z}/4 gradings for two-bridge knots, whose irreducible traceless characters are all binary dihedral, and for T(3,n)T(3,n), where at most one is. We also give a proof through Khovanov homology, using Schütz’s computation for three-braids, of Li and Ye’s computation of the rank of the instanton homology of T(3,n)T(3,n), and compare the differential of the knot 8198_{19} with the single pillowcase bigon of Hedden, Herald and Kirk.

papers.label: Instanton homology of knots
papers.abstract_html: Hedden, Herald and Kirk conjectured that every knot admits a decomposition along a Conway sphere for which the Lagrangian Floer homology of the two associated immersed curves in the pillowcase recovers Kronheimer and Mrowka’s reduced singular instanton homology. We prove the conjecture for the hyperbolic pretzel knots P(−2,3,q)P(-2,3,q); it was previously known for two-bridge knots and for some torus knots. The decomposition is obtained from Hedden, Herald and Kirk’s decomposition of the torus knot T(3,5)T(3,5) by Dehn twists along the Conway sphere, which act on the pillowcase by a linear shear. Building on our analysis of the torus knots T(3,n)T(3,n), we compute the Floer complex and its ℤ/4\mathbb{Z}/4 grading by hand; its differential is nonzero for every member of the family except P(−2,3,7)P(-2,3,7). The same method proves the conjecture for a family of twisted torus knots, under a hypothesis on the chirality of the torus-knot decomposition. On the instanton side, we show that the instanton homology of P(−2,3,q)P(-2,3,q) is free abelian of rank q+2q+2 for every odd q≥3q\ge3, extending Lobb and Zentner’s rational computation to the integers by means of Manion’s integral Khovanov homology; for the hyperbolic members this also follows from work of Daemi and Scaduto.

papers.label: Instanton homology of knots
papers.abstract_html: Cazassus, Herald, Kirk and Kotelskiy conjectured that the reduced singular instanton homology of a knot is recovered from any decomposition along a Conway sphere by Lagrangian Floer homology in the pillowcase, once the immersed curves of the two tangles carry suitable bounding cochains. For Smith’s decomposition of the pretzel knots P(−2,3,q), which separates a rational tangle carrying the earring from the sum of two other rational tangles, zero bounding cochains give the wrong rank. Working in the algebraic model of Kotelskiy, Watson and Zibrowius, where the Maurer–Cartan equation is a finite identity, we construct for P(−2,3,5) and P(−2,3,7) explicit Maurer–Cartan elements, each obtained by smoothing a model of Smith’s curve at a single self-intersection, that restore the rank. For P(−2,3,7), a second closure of the tangle selects one of them, conditionally on the conjecture and on a hypothesis about the support of the cochain. The resulting object is a rational arc together with a closed curve carrying a two-dimensional local system, and one further term near a corner turns it into the Bar-Natan invariant of the tangle. Granting one case of an intersection formula of Kotelskiy, Watson and Zibrowius, we show that no rational closure distinguishes the two. We ask whether the object that the conjecture assigns to this tangle is its Bar-Natan invariant, and record evidence on both sides.

papers.title: The S-complex differential of torus knots
papers.label: Instanton homology of knots
papers.abstract_html: For a torus knot K=T(p,q) the traceless SU(2) character variety is finite and nondegenerate, so Daemi and Scaduto’s S-complex for singular instanton homology can be built on it. The resulting complex has rank 1+|σ(K)|, where σ is the signature, and by theorems of Li and Ye and of Kronheimer and Mrowka its homology I♮(K) has rank ‖ΔK‖1, the sum of the absolute values of the coefficients of the Alexander polynomial; so the differential has rank R(p,q)=12(1+|σ|−‖Δ‖1). We express R(p,q) through floor sums and show that, for coprime 2≤p<q, R(p,q)≥⌊(p−2b)2/4⌋, where b∈{1,…,p−1} is the inverse of q modulo p, and that the differential vanishes if and only if p=2, or p is odd and q≡2 or q≡p+2(−1)(p−1)/2(mod2p); the ‘if’ direction is due to Daemi and Scaduto. By a result of Daemi and Scaduto, the component of the differential to the reducible generator is nonzero over ℚ exactly when their invariant h is positive. We show that the components from degree 3 to degree 2 and from degree 1 to degree 0 have ranks ⌊R/2⌋ and ⌈R/2⌉, independently of the choices in the construction. In particular the ℤ/4-graded group I♮(T(p,q);ℚ) depends only on σ and ‖Δ‖1, and we give it explicitly. In each small-perturbation pillowcase computation of Hedden, Herald and Kirk, a bigon ends at the reducible generator exactly when h>0. We formulate a chain-level conjecture identifying the two complexes over F2; it predicts this pattern whenever the map to the reducible is nonzero modulo 2.

papers.title: Pillowcase Floer homology of the torus knots T(3,n)
papers.label: Instanton homology of knots
papers.abstract_html: Hedden, Herald and Kirk defined a Lagrangian Floer homology in the pillowcase from a tangle decomposition of a knot and conjectured that, for a suitable decomposition, it recovers reduced singular instanton homology. We compute this homology for every torus knot T(3,n), using their decomposition. For all sufficiently small holonomy perturbations in an explicit closed cone, the immersed curves are restricted and the complex has 1+|σ| generators, where σ is the signature. There is no differential when n≡1,2(mod6) and exactly one, to the generator of the abelian representation, when n≡4,5(mod6). The Z/4-graded homology has the graded dimensions of reduced instanton homology. This verifies the conjecture of Hedden, Herald and Kirk for this infinite family, and, combined with a cobordism inequality of Daemi and Scaduto, shows that over F2 the pillowcase complex is S-chain homotopy equivalent to their singular instanton S-complex. The proof rests on an explicit description of the traceless character variety and the strict monotonicity of an angle function along its components; three inequalities are verified by interval arithmetic. For a different decomposition of T(3,4) in the same family, a numerical computation gives homology of rank 7 rather than 5 with zero bounding cochain.

papers.abstract_html:
We prove compatibility of the integral point operations in the admissible SO(3) Atiyah–Floer comparison of Daemi, Fukaya, and Lipyanskiy, in their embedded-Lagrangian setting. In the positive p1 normalization, the symplectic point operation is shifted by 8, 4, or 0 according as the marked component has genus one, two, or at least three. One coherent orientation system works for both matching components. Together with the known surface and loop comparisons and integral operation relations, this gives the corrected observable-algebra action over every commutative coefficient ring. When four is invertible, quarter-Pontryagin normalization gives the shifts 2, 1, and 0.

An index-four mixed sequence can develop a matching bubble of normalized energy one-half. Holomorphic doubling and the converse estimates identify compact limiting models: degree-one stable families and single elementary modifications of constant families. A Dirichlet construction reconstructs these models and glues them to regular index-zero mixed solutions. Converse gluing and the incidence conditions identify every bubbling end of the chosen point cut. The relative incidence degrees are eight and four in genera one and two. Comparing the actual gluing derivative with determinant-line excision determines their signs. Ordinary reference orientations agree for the two homologous matching surfaces; a local sphere comparison and a stabilized torus example fix the genus-two normalization even when the ambient rational Floer homology vanishes. The resulting boundary identity uses the original integral geometric count as its homotopy.

papers.abstract_html: We prove that isomorphisms of the type constructed by Daemi, Fukaya and Lipyanskiy, between framed instanton homology and the Lagrangian Floer homology of a Heegaard splitting, intertwine the cobordism maps of Kronheimer and Mrowka with maps defined by holomorphic curves alone, over the field of two elements. This holds for every connected cobordism between connected three-manifolds carrying a framed arc between its ends and an SO(3) bundle trivialized along the ends and the arc. The symplectic maps count holomorphic triangles in moduli spaces of flat connections on surfaces, with the correspondence of a compression body as boundary condition for one- and three-handles. Consequently these maps are independent of the handle decomposition and of the Heegaard data, and form a functor isomorphic to framed instanton homology; where both are defined, our isomorphisms agree with those of Daemi, Fukaya and Lipyanskiy modulo two. The proof rests on two analytic results for the mixed anti-self-duality and holomorphic curve equation: an adiabatic limit in which a compression body collapses next to a holomorphic strip and becomes the Lagrangian boundary condition of its flat connections, and an excision theorem along a torus.

papers.abstract_html: We prove that the mixed isomorphisms of Daemi, Fukaya and Lipyanskiy type between framed instanton homology and the Lagrangian Floer homology of a Heegaard splitting intertwine the integral instanton cobordism maps, oriented by almost-complex structures, with signed symplectic cobordism maps, up to chain homotopy and one overall sign for each cobordism. This holds for every connected cobordism between connected three-manifolds carrying a framed arc and an SO(3) bundle trivialized along the ends and the arc. Where the integral framed instanton homology is nonzero, the symplectic maps are signed counts of holomorphic triangles, with the Lagrangian correspondence of a compression body as one boundary condition for one- and three-handles. At three-manifolds whose integral framed instanton homology vanishes, the complexes are contractible and the maps are zero. The orientations are transported from the gauge theory through the mixed anti-self-duality and holomorphic curve equation. Consequently these maps form a projective functor on homology, independent of the handle decomposition up to sign. The unsigned analysis is that of the comparison modulo two; the new input is that two degenerations of the mixed equation, the collapse of a compression body and excision along a torus, preserve orientations. Where this homology is nonzero, we also prove that the sign by which the orientations change when a sphere is attached to a strip is constant under small perturbations and invariant under reversing the splitting. The relation with homology-oriented integral instanton maps is left open.

papers.abstract_html: We construct integral chain homotopy equivalences intertwining the usual framed instanton cobordism maps in the singular Hopf-link construction with symplectic cobordism maps oriented by transport from gauge theory. At common regular small data, the equivalences are represented by the Daemi–Fukaya–Lipyanskiy mixed count with a specified coherent orientation. For connected framed cobordisms, they are natural up to integral chain homotopy and one overall sign, with an explicit grading conversion, and extend by geometric changes of presentation. We also construct equivalences to the normalization in which attachment of a generating sphere in the surface moduli space preserves orientation, for every closed connected oriented three-manifold. Surgery generation gives a finite model built from one-generator complexes for the three-sphere. Counts through the three-sphere realize its grading-preserving matrix entries, so an algebraically chosen normalization becomes a finite integer linear combination of products of geometric counts. A polynomial in forward and reflected mixed counts transfers this construction to the symplectic complex. The proof uses the companion analytic and naturality results and the stated ordinary surgery and oriented gluing inputs. Identification with prescribed relative-spin maps and the nonsingular cap convention remains open.

papers.abstract_html: We prove an oriented neighborhood theorem at the first Uhlenbeck level of SO(3)-monopole moduli spaces, over a compact regular Seiberg–Witten moduli space of arbitrary dimension whose solutions have nonzero spinor. A finite-dimensional obstruction model admits an equivariant compactified embedding that maps the obstruction zero set homeomorphically onto an Uhlenbeck-open neighborhood of the ideal stratum; its restriction to that zero set at positive scale is a diffeomorphism onto its image. The principal analytic step is a strong approximation theorem in critical norms for arbitrary convergent one-bubble monopole sequences. Uniform gauge estimates and summable decay along the neck recover the gluing parameters, including the relative frame, and give reverse uniqueness. A global equivariant stabilization treats the background family without requiring a constant-rank spectral cutoff. Comparison with Donaldson’s instanton-addition map identifies the induced orientation with the standard monopole orientation. Under the additional topological hypotheses of Feehan and Leness, the construction supplies the analytic neighborhood input to their level-one link pairing. We state the resulting polynomial formula and its low-degree consequences for Witten’s conjecture on abundant, effective manifolds of Seiberg–Witten simple type.

papers.abstract_html:
We construct smooth toric Fano nn-folds of Picard number n+2n+2 whose tangent bundles are slope-stable with respect to the anticanonical polarization, for every n≥4n\ge4. The construction gives toric fibrations with fibre the del Pezzo surface of degree six over products of projective lines, parametrized by multisets of roots of A2A_2. Every nonempty multiset of nonzero roots with vanishing sum yields a stable tangent bundle. Among these multisets, the resulting variety is Kähler–Einstein if and only if the multiset is invariant under negation or under the order-three rotation of the root hexagon. We also construct stable, non-Kähler–Einstein examples with nonzero twist sum in every even dimension at least four. The proofs reduce slope inequalities and barycenter computations to integrals over the moment hexagon.

For a smooth toric Fano variety with strictly semistable tangent bundle, we prove that polystability is equivalent to decomposition as a nontrivial product of smooth toric Fano varieties with anticanonically stable tangent bundles. Exact evaluation of Klyachko’s criterion extends the stability classification to dimensions five and six, recovering the classifications of Steffens and Reynolds in dimensions three and four. Together with the product criterion, this determines polystability for all 8,6308{,}630 varieties in dimensions three through six, and hence the existence of Hermitian–Einstein metrics on their tangent bundles with respect to an anticanonical Kähler form.

papers.abstract_html: For Fano blowups of products of projective spaces along invariant codimension-two centres indexed by a tree, using distinct coordinate hyperplanes at each factor, anticanonical tangent stability is equivalent to one divisor-degree inequality at each vertex. The exceptional contributions are mixed intersections on the blowup centres. Stability holds for every tree of maximum degree at most three whose nonleaf factor dimensions equal their valences, with arbitrary positive leaf dimensions. For smooth toric Fano varieties that are locally trivial toric bundles with fibre a product of degree-six del Pezzo surfaces and base a product of projective spaces, the largest Picard number compatible with tangent stability in dimension n≥4 is ⌊5n/4⌋+1, allowing arbitrary integral twists. Every fixed tree of maximum degree at most three with an edge yields bundles attaining this bound after sufficiently long independent edge subdivisions. Their number, up to isomorphism of toric fans, is unbounded as the dimension grows through multiples of four. The proofs use relative tangent bundles, ranks of subspaces spanned by rays, and integral comparisons. The bundle existence proofs also use finite exact rational calculations with uniform error estimates and induction.

papers.abstract_html:
We classify the anticanonical slope stability of the tangent bundles of Xp,q=ℙ(ℙ1)p+q(O⊕O(1p,−1q)), where p,q are nonnegative integers and p+q≥1. The tangent bundle is stable when p=q, strictly semistable when |p−q|=1, and unstable otherwise. For p=k and q=k−1, the germ of the semistable polarization locus at the anticanonical class is real analytically equivalent to [0,∞)k×ℝk, with stable locus (0,∞)k×ℝk. In particular, the number of independent local chamber boundaries is unbounded.

For a smooth projective toric variety whose tangent bundle is semistable at a polarization H0, we describe the local chamber at H0 by the order ideals of a finite poset determined by the equal-slope ray subspaces. If each such subspace is spanned by the rays it contains in every maximal cone, nearby stable polarizations exist precisely when the variety is not a nontrivial toric product. Applied to the existing anticanonical census in dimensions three through six, this criterion gives nearby stability in all 31 indecomposable strictly semistable cases, whose local chambers have one, two, or three independent boundaries. We determine locally free, pairwise nonisomorphic Jordan–Hölder factors both for these cases and for the family Xk,k−1.

papers.abstract_html: We construct projective Calabi–Yau threefolds with isolated Gorenstein canonical singularities that admit no smoothing, as anticanonical hypersurfaces in Gorenstein Fano toric fourfolds. One example has a unique singularity, the anticanonical cone over the first Hirzebruch surface. Another has a unique singularity whose reduced miniversal base is a smooth curve but whose deformations are all singular. The construction combines Altmann’s deformation theory with the smoothing criterion of Corti–Filip–Petracci: a two-dimensional face of the ambient fan polytope with primitive edges obstructs smoothing if it has no Minkowski decomposition into unit segments and unimodular triangles. We also classify the 217 isolated Gorenstein toric threefold singularities whose polygon edge vectors have coordinates in [−2,2][-2,2] in some lattice basis, recording their deformation types and smoothing components. A scan of the Kreuzer–Skarke classification finds this obstruction in 39,175,53639{,}175{,}536 of its 473,800,776473{,}800{,}776 polytopes (approximately 8.27%8.27\%), whose generic anticanonical hypersurfaces therefore admit no smoothing.

papers.abstract_html: Let Δ\Delta be a reflexive four-polytope with primitive edges. We construct deformations of the toric fourfold defined by its face fan that smooth the singularities of a generic anticanonical Calabi–Yau hypersurface over a chosen two-dimensional face. The construction applies when the face cone is smoothable and the dual edge has an interior lattice point; its equations are trinomials in Cox coordinates. It gives a smoothing of the hypersurface when this is the only face whose cone is singular. If every singular face satisfies these conditions, simultaneous smoothing follows in the nodal case and, in general, under irreducibility of the semiuniversal deformation space. A seven-vertex example with one ordinary double point and no smoothing shows that the dual-edge condition is sharp. A scan of the Kreuzer–Skarke classification shows that the facewise criterion accounts for 3,774 of the 30,241 smoothings in the Batyrev–Kreuzer census; the other 26,467 require relations among exceptional curve classes from different faces.

papers.abstract_html: We classify reflexive four-polytopes for which the generic anticanonical hypersurfaces associated with the face fans of the polytope and its polar both have at most isolated singularities. There are exactly 590 such polytopes up to lattice equivalence in the Kreuzer–Skarke classification. Their two-dimensional faces belong to twelve lattice-isomorphism classes, all triangles, zonotopes, or reflexive polygons. The only nonsmoothable local models are the cyclic quotients 13(1,1,1)\frac13(1,1,1) and 15(1,1,3)\frac15(1,1,3) and the anticanonical cone over the first Hirzebruch surface; no singularity has a positive-dimensional reduced deformation space without a smoothing component. Within this classification, the Hirzebruch cone occurs in a unique mirror pair, associated with polytopes having 22 and 26 vertices. We exhibit this pair explicitly: one hypersurface is nonsmoothable, while all singularities of its mirror are locally smoothable. The crepant resolutions have Hodge numbers (20,26)(20,26) and (26,20)(26,20). At the opposite extreme, the self-dual 24-cell is the unique member of the classification for which both hypersurfaces are smooth before crepant resolution.

papers.abstract_html: We prove a homological obstruction to smoothing projective Calabi–Yau threefolds with nodes and anticanonical cones over smooth del Pezzo surfaces of degrees six and seven. On a crepant resolution that is small over the nodes and blows up the cone vertices, any smoothing forces a relation among link classes bounding in the local Milnor fibers. The relation is nonzero at every node and degree-seven point, and at each degree-six point smoothed through the one-dimensional component. The proof uses vanishing periods and applies to smoothing arcs of arbitrary contact order, extending the necessity direction of Friedman’s criterion. We apply the obstruction to a Batyrev hypersurface whose thirty singularities are individually smoothable but which admits no smoothing, even formally. On its mirror partner, two nodes cannot be smoothed by any analytic deformation, independently of a locally nonsmoothable cone point.

papers.abstract_html: We give a necessary and sufficient homological criterion for smoothing projective Calabi–Yau threefolds with nodes and anticanonical cones over smooth del Pezzo surfaces of degrees five, six and seven, or over a smooth quadric surface. For some choice of local smoothing components, the criterion requires a relation on a crepant resolution among link classes whose associated local parameters avoid every discriminant. The complexified relation space describes first-order deformations modulo locally trivial ones. Necessity follows from local period and vanishing-cycle arguments; sufficiency applies Friedman's unobstructedness theorem to a crepant partial resolution. Whenever the criterion holds, the deformation space on the chosen components is smooth. A nonsmoothable example, whose deformation space is reduced with four smooth components, shows why nonvanishing at every singular point is insufficient. We also construct a smoothable Batyrev hypersurface admitting no smoothing induced by proper ambient families obtained from Minkowski decompositions at a single lattice degree.

In an explicit four-node family, every member of the unique codimension-three nodal component admits a projective small resolution. For general members, these resolutions are birational to Batyrev mirrors of smoothings of the original nodal threefold, giving the reversed transition predicted by Morrison in this family.

papers.abstract_html: For projective conifold transitions of Calabi–Yau threefolds, we lift the numerical degeneration formula to Pardon's rational universal curve-counting algebra. We assume a smoothing with smooth algebraic total space and torsion-free second homology at both endpoints. Together with a finite genus-zero mirror calculation, this bound determines all 37 candidate universal coefficients: eight are nonzero, and their sum agrees with an independent stable-pair calculation on a plane in the smoothing. We also determine the smoothing coefficient in twice the line class. If the resolution has integral product exponents, then so does the smoothing.

papers.abstract_html: We construct a smooth projective Calabi–Yau threefold with torsion-free second homology whose product expansion in Pardon's scalar equivariant local-curve generators has a nonintegral exponent. The genus-ten exponent at three times a primitive class has fractional part 23, disproving the integer-exponent assertion for these generators. We realize a count violating this condition on a first Hirzebruch surface in a compact toric hypersurface. A filtration by powers of the surface ideal controls transverse thickenings and disconnected products; the stable-pair moduli space at minimal Euler characteristic is a projective space of dimension thirteen, with virtual count −14. The proof bounds the critical graphs, which carry the jumps, by the central charge and passes to the invariants through the wall-crossing group. Whenever a critical graph has one boundary marking of each type, this group acts simply transitively only after the vector field of the anti-diagonal torus action is adjoined. Beyond the simple range, dependence first appears with two interior insertions when both exponents are at least four and with three otherwise, while one insertion of descendent degree one produces wall-crossing for every pair. At central charge one every primary wall generator is a multiple of the torus vector field. A B-model analogue, for open Saito potentials, is due to Maher.

papers.abstract_html: For the genus-zero open FJRW invariants of Gross, Kelly and Tessler attached to a two-variable Fermat polynomial, we prove that the wall-crossing transformation between the two extremal systems of invariants factors uniquely, in every finite truncation, into automorphisms supported on rays in the quadrant of boundary-marking numbers, ordered by slope. In these two systems, within each set of invariants mixed by wall-crossing, all vanish except the one with the fewest, respectively most, boundary markings of the first type. Each critical graph contributes a generator on the ray of its boundary-marking numbers, the only ray whose monomials that generator fixes. The proof combines the Kontsevich–Soibelman ordered-product lemma, run with a filtration in place of a grading, with the simply transitive action of the wall-crossing group enlarged by a torus direction. The factorization is realized ray by ray by concatenated homotopies of boundary conditions, though in general not by a single homotopy from the extension lemma of Gross, Kelly and Tessler. Finally, in each truncation the potentials between consecutive rays are transported from one set of initial coefficients, analogous to theta-function coefficients, which can be nonzero on terms with several internal markings.

papers.abstract_html: We study the small eigenvalues of the Dolbeault Laplacian on trace-free endomorphisms of a semistable holomorphic bundle along Hermitian Yang–Mills flow, normalized as h−1∂τh=−2(Kh−κ) with Kh the mean curvature and κ its average. The bundles considered are simple bundles on a compact curve whose Jordan–Hölder factors are pairwise nonisomorphic, and extensions of one polystable bundle by another on compact Kähler manifolds, again with pairwise nonisomorphic stable factors. From every smooth initial metric, each small eigenvalue is asymptotic to an eigenvalue of a weighted graph Laplacian, whose conductances evolve by an explicit finite-dimensional flow; the relative error tends to zero. The graph records which stable factors are joined by nonzero extension classes. The asymptotics are governed by the weight grading of Haiden, Katzarkov, Kontsevich, and Pandit, the solution of a quadratic program on this graph. Suppose some Lagrange multiplier vector of this program is strictly positive on every active constraint. We then determine the decay exponent and the leading coefficient of every small eigenvalue, and the limits of the spectral subspaces. The eigenvalues of order τ−1 have coefficients independent of the initial metric, and 1/2 is always one of them. At each faster rate the coefficients depend on the initial metric, and their sum is unbounded over metrics on one fixed bundle. A key step shows that the bounded remainder in the asymptotics of the finite-dimensional flow converges. Examples include an eigenvalue decaying like τ−4/3 and, without the positivity condition, an eigenvalue of order (τlogτ)−1. We also treat families of harmonic extensions with fixed metrics, including repeated factors and recovery of the graded object, and we show that the constants in a slope inequality relating the lowest eigenvalue to the averaged trace-free mean curvature are sharp in every rank.

We determine the small spectrum of the Dolbeault Laplacian on trace-free endomorphisms of Hermitian–Einstein bundles near intersections of slope-stability walls. On a compact Kähler manifold of dimension at least two, consider an extension of ⨁j=1kFj by F0, where the factors are pairwise nonisomorphic and stable of equal slope at the limiting Kähler class, and every extension component is nonzero. Write ri=rkFi and let ϵj be the Einstein constant of Fj minus that of the extension. In the chamber ϵj>0, exactly k eigenvalues tend to zero. They agree, to relative error O(∑jϵj), with the eigenvalues of diag(ϵ1,…,ϵk)+r0−1vv*, where vj=rjϵj. The estimate is uniform in all positive ratios of the slope gaps. Thus the ranks and slopes determine the leading spectrum even when the gaps vanish at arbitrarily different rates.

For two factors we obtain λ1=δ−Dδ2+o(δ2), where δ>0 is the quotient Einstein constant minus the subbundle Einstein constant and D≥0 is given by the Green operator of the graded connection. After rescaling the extension and making unitary identifications with the graded limit, we determine the normalized first eigensection through order δ in every spatial Cm norm. Toric tangent bundles provide examples with arbitrarily many small eigenvalues whose orders of vanishing can be prescribed independently.

The proof uses curvature identities across graph cuts to control the nonlinear correction at each vanishing scale. As consequences, we obtain a relative approximation of the metric and a spanning-tree formula for the leading vanishing factor of the zeta-regularized determinant. papers.abstract_html: We construct smooth projective toric varieties with nonsimplicial local slope-stability chambers for their tangent bundles. In every even dimension 2k+2≥4, a fibre product of two projective-line bundles over (ℙ1)2k admits an ample real class at which the tangent bundle is strictly semistable. We also prove a local normal form at any ample real class where the tangent bundle of a smooth projective toric variety is semistable. It retains precisely the slope directions realized by polarizations, requires no local-freeness assumption on equal-slope subsheaves, and localizes every nearby Harder–Narasimhan filtration to their equality lattice. If the fan rays in each equal-slope subspace positively span that subspace, every centered slope direction occurs. papers.abstract_html: We study the natural L2 metric near a central Yang–Mills connection on a closed surface. In the classical quadratic symplectic model, we prove a relative metric estimate with error quadratic in the harmonic deformation parameter, uniformly across all stabilizer types. We also compute the leading metric correction using the Green operators of the reference connection. The proof first eliminates the gauge directions with a fixed positive spectral gap and then minimizes over the remaining finite-dimensional orbit; it requires no lower bound on a positive orbit eigenvalue. The same argument compares every small eigenvalue of the gauge Laplacian with the infinitesimal stabilizer-action operator, including at changes of kernel dimension. As a curved finite-dimensional comparison, quaternionic projective and hyperbolic reductions admit exact orbit-metric formulas on their flat moment-map zero cone. A four-cycle is realized in both settings with independently vanishing weights. The resulting estimates distinguish uniform control of the quotient metric from estimates that depend on the smallest orbit scale.

Donaldson, Seiberg–Witten, Floer, and Gromov–Witten theories extract invariants or algebraic structures from compactified moduli spaces. We study the inverse problem: which prescribed gluing data and algebraic identities can be realized by compactified moduli spaces, and when can such a realization arise from Fredholm geometry? The formulation uses decorated Feynman categories, marked realization categories, and smoothing profiles that distinguish boundary, real-normal, and complex-normal degenerations.

The principal result is an obstruction to extending stabilizing bundles across the associahedron K4. A compatible family over K2 and K3 extends if and only if its glued boundary bundle extends over K4; reflecting one endpoint identification produces a Möbius summand on ∂K4 and hence a nonextendable datum. We also prove that the equations d2=0 and the A∞ relations are precisely oriented filling conditions in dimension one, with higher extensions obstructed by ordinary smooth θ-bordism classes. Realization categories form fibers of a cartesian fibration over gluing data, and rigid realizations satisfy descent over overlapping color sets.

Family-index, compactness, and determinant-line conditions yield further obstructions to Fredholm realization; we examine them in flow, planar, stable-curve, and stable-disk examples. The resulting framework is a sequence of realization and obstruction problems, not a universal existence theorem.

papers.abstract_html: Complex deformations of noncompact canonical Calabi–Yau threefold singularities encode Higgs-branch renormalization-group flows of five-dimensional theories. We determine which such flows remain available when several singularities occur in one compact Calabi–Yau threefold. The local sectors are conifold points supporting free hypermultiplets and cones over smooth del Pezzo surfaces of degrees five, six and seven, and over P1×P1 of degree eight, engineering the rank-one E4,E3,E2,E1 fixed points. We identify their deformation coordinates with flavor moment maps and derive a compact Abelian gauging matrix from wrapped-M2 charges and divisor pairings. On every choice of local Higgs components, we prove that the invariant deformation-coordinate values attained on the triplet moment-map zero locus in the rigid description are precisely the kernel of this matrix. For connected normal projective threefolds with these exact analytic germs, trivial canonical bundle, h1(O)=0, and a smooth projective crepant resolution of the specified local type, the same kernel is the image of the global first-order deformation space. Combining this identification with the mixed smoothing theorem gives a necessary and sufficient criterion: the kernel must meet the complement of every local discriminant. On the two-dimensional E3 component this requires three separate nonzero coefficients; at E4 it requires five nonzero conic-pencil pairings, identified integrally with the SU(5) diagonal moment-map coordinates. The selected global deformation base is smooth when its relation space projects nontrivially to each selected E3 summand; every tangent on that base integrates to a convergent deformation. Examples distinguish a joint conifold–E2 transition, sectors forced to remain undeformed, and nonzero E3 deformations forced to retain a singularity. These results concern geometric smoothing and invariant moment-map coordinates, not the full finite-Planck hypermultiplet geometry.

papers.abstract_html: We study an explicit compact Calabi–Yau transition in which two conifold sectors and a rank-one E2 sector can Higgs only together. The integral relation between their curve classes determines two shared Abelian gaugings and a transition from Hodge numbers (6,122) to (3,123). We compute the primitive surviving charge lattice and its cubic couplings, and show that the flavor gauging cannot remain dynamical in a gravity-decoupling limit with bounded local Kähler scales. On an auxiliary circle the quantum transition contains four conifold states spanning a primitive rank-three electric lattice. Their one-loop thresholds reproduce the integral conifold monodromies. An explicit Laurent mutation and analytic continuation of all eight regular periods identify the genus-zero prepotential of the surviving vectors with that of the smooth phase, including the integral normalization and constant term, and hence its scalar and electromagnetic couplings. At fixed five-dimensional Planck scale the auxiliary-circle limit retains finite bulk gauging, but its closing Kaluza–Klein gap leaves the four conifold states no radius-independent energy range. This limit ends where the del Pezzo surface collapses. On the adjacent face of the nef cone, where only the two nodal curves and two exceptional curves of the del Pezzo surface have zero area, the same four states are massless hypermultiplets of five-dimensional M-theory. The K3 and elliptic fibrations identify a dilaton gauging, an anomaly-consistent six-dimensional U(2) phase and equal compact images of two E-string roots. An exact volume bound excludes the six-dimensional limit on the transition face. A heterotic K3 candidate and topological data are obtained; the global bundle construction and the finite-Planck hypermultiplet geometry remain open.

Fixed-support Hilbert schemes give rank-one numerical Donaldson–Thomas contributions on the rigid F1 and P2 surfaces on the two sides. On a reducible moving divisor, two dual-ideal sheaves are isolated and Gieseker stable, each contributing +1; their stability persists along ample polarizations approaching the contraction. Their vanishing first and second self-Ext groups also imply local persistence in smooth polarized deformations of the resolved threefold, but not across its singular transition. An explicit magnetic splitting has one extension mode and a transverse phase alignment near large volume. Using the analytically continued periods of the companion paper, we determine the constituent phase sign at the marked quantum transition and exclude emission of the known light electric particles on a final specified segment. The probe charges nevertheless carry confined magnetic flux after Higgsing. These are component counts and partial wall constraints, not a determination of the physical BPS index at the endpoint. papers.abstract_html: When a compact Calabi–Yau threefold degenerates, M-theory on it acquires light charged hypermultiplets whose condensation opens a Higgs branch, locally a hyperkähler quotient without gravity. At finite Planck mass the hypermultiplet moduli space is quaternionic Kähler, its metric is unknown, and its moment maps have no additive constant, hence no Fayet–Iliopoulos parameter. We prove a local normal form for quaternionic Kähler quotients near a fixed point at which the moment map vanishes, under a freeness condition on the normal representation: the quotient is locally the product of the fixed set with the flat hyperkähler quotient of that representation, with relative metric corrections of order r2 at distance r. Consequently, if exactly k disjoint (−1,−1)-curves have zero area on a face of the nef cone with finite gauge couplings, and their classes satisfy one primitive relation ∑iai[Ci]=0 with all ai≠0, then, under a regularity hypothesis on the effective supergravity, the Higgs branch opened by the k light hypermultiplets is locally a smooth factor times C2/Zm, m=∑i|ai|, as without gravity. Transverse to the smooth factor, the order-r2 correction is the curvature of the hypermultiplet manifold restricted to a quaternionic line. A transition with two nodes and a cone over the degree-seven del Pezzo surface has such a face with k=4, giving C2/Z4; where the del Pezzo surface collapses, the Higgs branch defined as the metric completion of the vacua on the smoothed threefold is again of this form. In type IIA string theory, under corresponding hypotheses, the C2/Zk point that Greene, Morrison and Vafa expected near k homologous vanishing three-cycles persists at finite Planck mass for these smoothings. A census of toric hypersurfaces finds 5605 faces whose light spectrum has one relation, 372 with k≥3, all with m=k.

papers.abstract_html: In the west-coast model of black hole evaporation, the diagonal approximation computes the entropy of the radiation near the Page time by averaging the entropy of fixed-area states over the black hole’s fluctuating area. We show that this approximation, written level by level, misses an order-one constant: as the area distribution becomes broad, whatever its shape, the exact entropy exceeds it by −qlog⁡q-q\log q, where qq is the canonical probability that the black hole is larger than the radiation. The constant arises because the radiation, which has no energy of its own, can resolve area sectors only through the island, and so not those in which the black hole is larger than itself. For a symmetric distribution the excess is half of log⁡2\log 2 at the Page point and largest after it, so the exact transition is asymmetric. The proof reduces the entropy of the exact planar spectrum, a free multiplicative convolution, to a single integral. We compute the first correction and evaluate the constant in Jackiw–Teitelboim gravity. At fixed area, the two-saddle truncation misses the Rényi moments by Catalan factors.

papers.abstract_html: Thermodynamic fluctuations smooth Page transitions, but the usual Gaussian description fails at a black-hole critical point. We determine the resulting finite-size crossover in a canonical random-pure-state model whose density of states is specified by the Reissner–Nordström–AdS entropy. In four or more bulk dimensions, the critical fluctuations obey a quartic limiting law, and the transition width grows as the three-quarter power of the critical black-hole entropy. We derive the leading transition profile and its temperature dependence, and identify the reservoir heat capacity required to preserve the canonical critical behavior. Regular-phase examples provide a comparison with Gaussian fluctuations. The entanglement results hold in the planar limit of the specified random-state model; applications to gravitational entropy transitions require identifying the corresponding state and the fluctuating difference of generalized entropies.

papers.title: The Page Curve Is Not Enough: Universality, Ensemble Dependence, and Microscopic Ambiguity in Black Hole Information Recovery
papers.label: Black hole information
papers.abstract_html: A Page curve constrains radiation entanglement, but its implications for microscopic information recovery depend on which state, ensemble, and channel data are specified. We examine this dependence through explicit finite-dimensional constructions and controlled random-state limits. Two density-matrix ensembles can have the same averaged spectral measure, every averaged replica moment, and the same mean von Neumann entropy, while their entropy and purity fluctuations differ. Fixed Marchenko–Pastur spectra and normalized Wishart spectra give a related large-dimension comparison. At the channel level, an isometry and a replacement channel can reproduce the complete nested radiation trajectory for one input while having different correlations with an external reference. For normalized states, annealed and quenched Rényi entropies have the same von Neumann limit; the derivative of their finite-order difference measures the entropy variance. We derive normalized replica-covariance identities and illustrate their normalization with the standard Haar purity covariance, separating these quantities from entropy of an averaged state. Finally, Gaussian and quartic fluctuations with equal variance give different entropy-transition profiles, illustrating the additional role of joint branch fluctuations and reservoir constraints. These calculations delimit what entropy and spectral agreement establish and specify further comparisons needed in gravitational models.

papers.catalogue_title: From Hawking to Marchenko–Pastur: A Guide to the Page Curve and Beyond
papers.title: From Hawking to Marchenko–Pastur: A Guide to the Page Curve and Beyond
papers.label: Black hole information
papers.abstract_html: This tutorial develops the Page curve program from quantum entanglement and Hawking radiation to holographic entropy, replica wormholes, and random matrix theory. We derive the normalized random-state benchmark and its Marchenko–Pastur limit, explaining the roles of non-crossing partitions and spectral resolvents. We then distinguish averaging conditional entropies from calculating the entropy of a state with fluctuating energy or area. Gaussian broadening, finite reservoirs, and a quartic critical model illustrate how the preparation and the fluctuation law enter this distinction. Exact finite-dimensional examples separate averaged spectra from ensemble fluctuations and radiation data for one input from information about a quantum channel. Normalized annealed and quenched Rényi entropies have a common von Neumann limit, while their finite-order difference and connected replica moments measure additional ensemble information. Throughout, explicit calculations are distinguished from gravitational applications that require further assumptions. The resulting account provides a self-contained introduction to the established methods and to the remaining questions about microscopic information recovery.

papers.title: Informational Singularities and the Completion of Gravity: Replica Wormholes, Indeterminism, and Cosmic Censorship
papers.label: Black hole information
papers.abstract_html: Replica wormholes provide the first concrete evidence that quantum gravity can achieve informational completion-restoring a unique, coherent mapping from initial to final quantum states-without achieving geometric completion, the removal or resolution of curvature singularities. I make this distinction precise and use it to extend the framework of generalized indeterminism developed by Azhar and Namjoo into the quantum-gravitational regime. I introduce the concept of an informational singularity: a configuration in which a physical theory fails to provide an existent, unique, and coherent mapping from initial to final quantum states. This concept is logically independent of the geometric singularities of general relativity. The two notions can come apart in both directions: a geometrically smooth region (such as the asymptotic radiation zone in Hawking's calculation) can be informationally singular, while a region with a curvature singularity (such as the interior of an evaporating black hole described by the Page curve) can be informationally complete. I show that the island formula and replica wormhole construction realize informational completion while leaving the geometric singularity untouched, and I confront the ensemble interpretation of the gravitational path integral as a possible obstruction to single-theory completion. Finally, I propose a reformulation of strong cosmic censorship as Informational Cosmic Censorship: the principle that the full quantumgravitational theory provides a coherent state map for generic initial data, regardless of the geometric fate of Cauchy horizons. I argue that this reformulation captures Penrose's original predictability motivation more faithfully than the standard geometric formulation.

papers.title: Prediction Markets as the Informational Substrate of the Machine Economy
papers.label: AI and the machine economy
papers.abstract_html: Wuebben [2026] identified six institutional primitives required for autonomous machine-to-machine commerce and showed that three-adjudication, reputation, and liability/insurance exhibit critical gaps that constrain the machine economy's emergence. This paper argues that all three gaps share a common root: the absence of market-generated price signals for agent performance risk, deliverable quality, and failure correlation. Meanwhile, the settlement layer has matured faster than anticipated: three competing protocol standards-Stripe's Agentic Commerce Protocol, Coinbase's x402, and the Machine Payments Protocol launched by Stripe and Tempo-have entered production within six months, confirming that the execution substrate for machine-to-machine payments is commoditizing rapidly. The widening asymmetry between settlement maturity and trust-layer immaturity sharpens the need for mechanisms that produce the missing information. We propose that prediction markets-generalized beyond event contracts to encompass continuous distributional forecasting in the spirit of Cotton [2022]-can serve as a cross-cutting informational layer that produces the missing inputs for the primitives that currently lack them. We design five specific market mechanisms, each targeting a gap in the original stack: Quality Adjudication Markets for escrowed deliverables, Agent Performance Futures for bonding and reputation, Correlation Discovery Markets for insurance pricing, Identity Assurance Markets for Sybil detection, and Primitive Readiness Markets for sequencing strategy. We analyze the incentive compatibility, liquidity requirements, manipulation resistance, and regulatory classification of each design. Drawing on Cotton [2022]'s microprediction architecture which collapses identity, reputation, and bonding into a single performance-scored object we propose a unified design pattern in which prediction market participation itself generates the data on which the institutional stack depends, partially dissolving the bootstrapping problem identified in the original paper. We assess the limits of the approach, identify the residual problems that prediction markets cannot solve, and propose a phased implementation path that builds directly on the settlement infrastructure now in production.

papers.title: The Institutional Plumbing for a Machine Economy: A Readiness Assessment of Building Blocks, Missing Infrastructure, and Commercial Opportunities
papers.label: AI and the machine economy
papers.abstract_html: Autonomous AI agents are approaching the capability threshold required to transact, negotiate, and settle economic obligations without human intermediation. But capability is not sufficiency. A functioning machine economy requires institutional infrastructure-identity, bonding, escrow, adjudication, settlement, reputation, and liability assignment-analogous to the legal and financial plumbing that enables human commerce. This paper audits each layer of that stack against current technological readiness, identifies the critical gaps, and evaluates where commercial opportunities lie: in the plumbing itself, or in the application layer above it. We find that of the six primitives required for a functioning machine economy, one is production-ready (settlement), two are close (identity, bonding infrastructure), and three have critical gaps (adjudication, reputation, liability/insurance). The binding constraints are on the "trust layer"-the primitives that enable agents to interact with counterparties they have no prior relationship with and no human intermediary to fall back on. We map commercial opportunities across both the infrastructure and application layers, and propose a phased strategy that captures near-term application-layer value while accumulating the data and expertise needed for plumbing-layer opportunities as the market matures.

papers.catalogue_title: Material Deployment Power in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: How Physical Constraints Reshape International Order
papers.title: Material Deployment Power in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: How Physical Constraints Reshape International Order
papers.label: International relations and politics
papers.abstract_html:
Prevailing accounts of artificial intelligence in international relations treat AI primarily as an informational or cognitive technology, emphasizing data, algorithms, and innovation capacity as the central sources of advantage. This article challenges that view by arguing that large-scale AI deployment re-centers physical constraint as a determinant of power. Although AI expands informational capacity at unprecedented speed, its deployment depends on infrastructural systems - energy generation, transmission, conversion, cooling, and critical materials - that expand slowly, are politically mediated, and are unevenly distributed. As a result, competition over AI moves international politics into a constraint-dominated phase in which power is conditioned by the ability to convert technological potential into sustained economic and military capability.

The article advances four contributions. First, it introduces the concept of  material deployment power MDP, defined as the capacity to mobilize and scale the physical systems necessary to operationalize advanced technologies under conditions of rivalry - a concept distinct from Michael Mann's institutional "infrastructural power." Second, it develops a theoretical account of how material constraints generate systematic patterns of coercion, state - firm fusion, and selective cooperation, explaining the resurgence of mercantilist policies and supply-security clubs in the AI era. Third, it demonstrates through comparative analysis and detailed process tracing - examining cases including semiconductor export controls, hyperscaler energy strategies, and rare earth processing - that variation in material deployment capacity shapes AI deployment outcomes, trade and industrial policy, and alliance behavior independently of innovation leadership. Fourth, it extends the analysis to two underexplored domains: the emergence of energy-backed digital assets as instruments of monetary sovereignty, and the domestic political consequences of capital-intensive technological transitions that concentrate returns while displacing labor.

The argument has broader implications for international order. By binding advanced capabilities to slow-moving physical systems, AI re-materializes global politics, increasing sensitivity to chokepoints, fragmenting interdependence, and reshaping the foundations of deterrence and cooperation. Understanding the geopolitics of artificial intelligence therefore requires rethinking prevailing assumptions about scalability, substitution, and the relationship between technology and power in the twenty-first century.

papers.title: Algorithmic Plausible Deniability: The Structural Erosion of Deterrence in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
papers.label: International relations and politics
papers.abstract_html: Classical deterrence theory assumes that hostile actions can be attributed to identifiable actors whose intentions can be inferred and who can be credibly threatened with punishment. This article introduces Algorithmic Plausible Deniability APD: a structural condition in which the delegation of decisions to artificial intelligence systems generates persistent uncertainty over authorship and intent, thereby weakening deterrence even when states act rationally and prefer stability. Unlike strategic ambiguity, which actors choose, APD emerges endogenously from algorithmic delegation and persists independently of deception or bad faith. The article develops three contributions. First, it provides a theoretical account of how AI systems degrade the informational foundations of deterrence through mechanisms of delegation, opacity, and emergent behavior. Second, it identifies an Accountability Trilemma in which states cannot simultaneously achieve operational effectiveness, strategic flexibility, and clear attribution. Third, it demonstrates that APD creates asymmetric effects: hostile actions become more deniable while signals of restraint become less credible, systematically undermining escalation control. The argument has implications for cyber conflict, autonomous weapons governance, and crisis stability among technologically advanced states.
